items.title: StereoVLM: Binocular Vision-Language Models for Metric 3D Spatial Reasoning
items.summary_1line: Introduces StereoVLM, a binocular vision-language model trained hierarchically on calibrated stereo images, reporting 95.17% depth accuracy and a 66.98 object-level score on its new Stereo3D-Bench.
items.editor_note: 입력을 바꾸는 것으로 스레드를 연다. 스테레오 쌍과 메트릭 3D 추론용 새 벤치마크를 제시한다.

items.title: Parsing Visual Latents for Multimodal Spatial Reasoning
items.summary_1line: LatentParse is a training-free framework that uses an analyst VLM to parse CLIP, DINOv3 and VGGT features into a text report of spatial evidence, improving five VLMs by 0.7-2.4 points on three spatial benchmarks.
items.editor_note: 새 모델을 학습하는 대신 기존 VLM을 개선하는 학습이 필요 없는(training-free) 방식을 더한다.

items.title: Seeking in Space: Benchmarking Purposeful Active Exploration of Vision-Language Models for Spatial Reasoning
items.summary_1line: ActSpace-Bench is a benchmark of 994 spatial questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, testing whether VLMs actively seek evidence before answering; strongest models explore purposefully but lose evidence to limited memory.
items.editor_note: 정적 이미지에서 능동적 탐색으로 넘어가며, 제한된 메모리를 병목으로 지목한다.

editorial.tldr: Three arXiv papers in four days attack the same weakness: vision-language models that misjudge depth, distance, and layout. They share a theme rather than one event, starting with StereoVLM, which feeds calibrated stereo image pairs to a VLM for metric 3D reasoning.
editorial.whats_new: ActSpace-Bench tests whether VLMs explore a scene before answering 994 spatial questions; the strongest models explore purposefully but lose gathered evidence to limited memory.
editorial.why_it_matters: For agents that act on camera input, the papers point at three levers outside the base model: richer sensor input, extra vision encoders, and memory across exploration steps.
editorial.take_for_builders: If an agent answers spatial questions from images, log what it saw at each step and check whether the final answer uses it; ActSpace-Bench points at memory, not perception, as the failure point.

beats.headline: StereoVLM adds binocular input for metric depth
beats.summary: Trains on calibrated stereo pairs and reports 95.17% depth accuracy on its own Stereo3D-Bench.

beats.headline: LatentParse turns vision-encoder features into a text report
beats.summary: Training-free: an analyst VLM reads CLIP, DINOv3 and VGGT features, lifting five VLMs by 0.7-2.4 points.

beats.headline: ActSpace-Bench measures active exploration and finds a memory bottleneck
beats.summary: 234 episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes; evidence gathered while exploring is lost before the answer.

open_questions: Does StereoVLM's depth accuracy hold on a benchmark its authors did not build?
Do LatentParse's 0.7-2.4 point gains justify running an extra analyst VLM and three encoders per query?
Does adding explicit scene memory close the evidence-loss gap ActSpace-Bench reports?
